questions.q: In the Harborline Logistics case study, why is Maintenance_Request__c modeled as its own object in a master-detail relationship to Vehicle__c, rather than as extra fields on Vehicle__c?
options: Validation rules cannot reference fields on the same object
A single vehicle can have many maintenance events over its life, and fields on a record can't repeat
Master-detail relationships are required for all custom objects
Roll-up summary fields only work on standard objects
questions.explain: Because a vehicle accumulates many maintenance events over time, those events need their own records (one per event) related back to the vehicle — the classic signal for a child object rather than repeating fields.

questions.q: Why is Technician__c related to Maintenance_Request__c by lookup rather than master-detail?
options: Lookup relationships are always preferred over master-detail
Master-detail relationships cannot be created between two custom objects
Technician__c needs a roll-up summary field, which requires lookup
A technician's existence doesn't depend on any single maintenance request — it should be able to exist independently
questions.explain: Master-detail implies the child cannot exist without its master and is deleted along with it. A technician clearly should exist independent of any one repair record, which is exactly what a lookup relationship allows.

questions.q: Why does the case study use an approval process (rather than only a validation rule) to handle costly maintenance requests?
options: The requirement is specifically for a named human to review and sign off, with a visible decision and audit trail — exactly what an approval process is built for
Validation rules cannot reference numeric fields like Cost__c
Approval processes are required on every custom object by default
A validation rule would block ALL maintenance requests, not just costly ones
questions.explain: A validation rule can only block or allow a save — it can't route a record to a specific person for review. 'Someone checking it' requires the routing, locking, and audit trail an approval process provides.

questions.q: Why is a sharing rule needed in addition to Private OWD and the role hierarchy, to give the Fleet Director visibility into all maintenance requests?
options: Sharing rules are mandatory on every private object
Dispatchers sit in a separate branch of the role hierarchy, so role hierarchy alone wouldn't grant the Fleet Director visibility into their records
The Fleet Director's profile automatically grants access to every object
Roll-up summary fields require a sharing rule to calculate correctly
questions.explain: Role hierarchy only grants upward visibility within the same branch. A sharing rule is needed to reach records owned by users in a different branch, such as dispatchers reporting elsewhere.

questions.q: What is the actual skill this case study lesson says it's testing?
options: Memorizing the Harborline Logistics scenario exactly as presented
Knowing how to build a trucking fleet management system specifically
The ability to trace any given business request back to the specific tool/decision from the right chapter — not the specific scenario itself
Writing Apex code to replace all the declarative tools shown
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states the traceability of decisions back to the right chapter and tool — not the particular fictional scenario — is the transferable skill being demonstrated.
